div.head: II Cn 80.1
div.ab: ⁊ forgá ælc man minne huntnoð, locehwær ic hit gefriðod wylle habban, be fullan wite.
⁊ forgá ælc man minne huntnoð, lochwar ic hit gefriðod wille habban (on minon agenan), be fullan wite.
⁊ forga elc man minne huntað, lochwær ic hit gefriðod habben wille, be fullan wite.
Et abstineat omnis homo á uenariis meis, ubicumque pacem eis haberi uolo, super plenam witam.
Et omnes deuitent meam, ubicunque illam habere uoluero.
[80, 1] Et dimittat meam uenacionem, ubicumque illam pacificatam esse uolo, super plenam forisfacturam.
⁊ forgá ælc man minne huntnoð lochwar ic hit gefriðod wille habban [on minon agenan], be fullan wite.
And forga ælc man minne huntnoð, locehwær ic hit gefriðod wylle habban, be fullan wite.
Aber jedermann vermeide meine Jagd, wo immer ich sie [mit Forstbann] umfriedet haben will, bei vollem Strafgelde.
But let every man avoid my hunting, wherever I wish to have it protected [by forest-ban], on pain of the full fine.
But everyone, under pain of incurring the full penalty, shall avoid hunting on my preserves, wherever they may be.
And everyone is to avoid trespassing on my hunting, wherever I wish to have it preserved, on pain of full fine.
And let each person abstain from my hunting grounds, which I wish to be preserved, or incur the full penalty.
div.note: Liebermann prints in a footnote some additions on fishponds and dogs (80.1a–b) which MS T of the Quadripartitus adds here, about 1220.; BR: added from Gesetze I p. 367, October 2026 (MS Cons)
wylle habban: B adds on minon agenan in a sixteenth-century hand

Hier fügt T, f. 104v um 1220 zu: [80, 1a] Si quis furatus fuerit pisces in stagno, quod Angli dicunt fiscpol{a}, persoluat domino stagni despectum suum, quod Angli ofersaunesse{b} [dicunt zu ergänzen]. — [80, 1b] Si{c} quis canem, qui custodire domini sui caulas debet et lupum abigere, occiderit, persoluat domino canis VI sol. Canem quem Angli dicunt greihund{d}, qui nondum cepit leporem nec aliam bestiam, XL d. persoluat; si uero doctus est et cepit, LXXX d. reddat. Canem, qui in pluuia{e} sine alicuius cura uigilat, quem Angli dicunt renhund, XII d. Canis uero qui uocatur uealter{f} et Angli dicunt lanlegeran{g}, X sol. persoluatur. — [Um 1320 copirt 80, 1b aus T ein Londoner, wahrscheinlich Andreas Horn, in die Hs. Co (der Or folgt) der Leges Angl. Lond. s. XIII. coll., ed. Liebermann p. 2. Er ändert öfters stilistisch, inhaltlich nur statt greihund fehlerhaft: greahund, id est canem de Grecia . . . X d. persoluat.]
a) Die Noten a—g beziehen sich auf Band II.

Here T, fol. 104v, c. 1220, adds: [80, 1a] Si quis furatus fuerit pisces in stagno, quod Angli dicunt fiscpol{a}, persoluat domino stagni despectum suum, quod Angli ofersaunesse{b} [dicunt to be supplied]. — [80, 1b] Si{c} quis canem, qui custodire domini sui caulas debet et lupum abigere, occiderit, persoluat domino canis VI sol. Canem quem Angli dicunt greihund{d}, qui nondum cepit leporem nec aliam bestiam, XL d. persoluat; si uero doctus est et cepit, LXXX d. reddat. Canem, qui in pluuia{e} sine alicuius cura uigilat, quem Angli dicunt renhund, XII d. Canis uero qui uocatur uealter{f} et Angli dicunt lanlegeran{g}, X sol. persoluatur. — [C. 1320 a Londoner, probably Andreas Horn, copied 80, 1b from T into MS Co (which Or follows) of the Leges Angl. Lond. s. XIII. coll., ed. Liebermann p. 2. He often alters the style, but the content only where, instead of greihund, he has erroneously: greahund, id est canem de Grecia . . . X d. persoluat.]
a) Notes a–g refer to vol. II.

In this case the full penalty probably means 120 shillings, the fine for insubordination to the king.
